article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Green Lantern × Ridgeline Runtz
Breeder: Ridgeline Farms
THC Content: 24–30%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: limonene , linalool , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Purple candy, grape, tropical fruit, pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 7–8 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: September through early October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: Medium to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Lantz carries the fingerprints of Southern Humboldt in a way few modern marijuana strains can imitate. Instead of beginning as a laboratory-designed commercial cross, it emerged from years of family breeding at Ridgeline Farms, where Jason Gellman and his father worked through generations of plants to combine two of their most successful cultivars. The finished weed can look almost unreal: rigid purple flowers, dense trichome coverage, flashes of forest green, and a surface that appears dusted with sugar. Its aroma moves from purple candy and ripe grape toward earthy pine and fuel, while the smoke often finishes with a creamy Kush character. That combination of old-school Humboldt gas and newer candy genetics helped Lantz stand out quickly, and its 2023 Emerald Cup victories transformed it from a regional craft cultivar into one of Ridgeline Farms’ defining strains.
Genetics and Lineage

Lantz was created by Ridgeline Farms from Green Lantern and Ridgeline Runtz. That direct parentage is confirmed by the farm itself and by its commercial collaboration with Cookies. The project took more than four years of crossing and phenotype selection, with the Gellman family repeatedly growing out offspring until they found the expression that eventually became Lantz. Rather than purchasing fashionable genetics and releasing a quick F1, Ridgeline developed the cultivar from two plants already established within its own award-winning cannabis program.

Green Lantern contributes the sharper side of the cross. Ridgeline describes that strain as intensely gassy, with a Sour Diesel -like aromatic character, floral overtones, substantial potency, and Kush-like strength. The farm also acknowledges that its exact deeper genetics remain something of a mystery, so highly specific pedigrees sometimes assigned to Green Lantern should not be treated as established breeder fact. Ridgeline Runtz supplies a contrasting profile of dark fruit, candy sweetness, purple coloration, and heavy resin production. It won first place in the sungrown flower category at the 2019 Emerald Cup, one year after Green Lantern took the licensed sungrown title.

Bringing those two champions together produced a hybrid that retained attributes from both without simply tasting like another Runtz cross. Purple fruit and candy are obvious, but pine, earth, and gas remain unusually persistent. Lantz has since become a major breeding parent for Ridgeline Farms, appearing in cultivars such as Ridgelion, Ridgeline Rebel, Plantz, Lamboz, Ridgeline Rose, and several other newer projects.
Effects and Experience

The high often begins with a clean mental shift rather than an immediate heavy body sensation. Mood rises, sensory details become more pronounced, and conversation or music can seem considerably more engaging. There is enough cerebral clarity early on that many experienced consumers find moderate amounts compatible with creative work, social settings, gaming , or an afternoon spent outdoors. The onset can be strong, however, especially when flower tests near the upper end of its typical THC range.

Physical relaxation enters later and develops gradually. Instead of shutting down mental activity, the body begins to feel looser while the euphoric headspace remains intact. The result can feel unusually functional for weed with such substantial potency. As consumption increases, that balance shifts: the limbs become heavier, motivation falls, and the experience takes on more of the calming, indica-leaning quality associated with Ridgeline Runtz and Kush-influenced cannabis.

Larger servings can become considerably stronger than the sweet flavor suggests. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, temporary memory impairment, anxiety, or excessive sedation are possible when THC intake exceeds personal tolerance. For inexperienced consumers, small amounts are the more sensible way to evaluate the strain.
Medical Benefits

The transition from cerebral elevation into deeper physical ease may appeal to some medical marijuana consumers who do not want their cannabis to begin with immediate sedation. The brighter opening can temporarily make everyday stress feel less intrusive, while the later body relaxation may be useful for people who already use THC-rich weed when trying to unwind after physical or mental strain.

Some consumers also choose potent hybrid cannabis for appetite stimulation, nausea, discomfort, or difficulty relaxing at night. Lantz can move toward those effects as the dose rises, although its relatively lucid beginning means the experience is not identical to a conventional heavy nighttime indica. Individual batches and personal tolerance can make a considerable difference.

Lantz itself has not been tested in controlled clinical trials as a treatment for pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another specific medical condition. Anyone using marijuana therapeutically should rely on laboratory results from the actual product rather than a strain name alone and should discuss cannabis use with a qualified healthcare professional when prescription medications or significant health conditions are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweet purple candy is one of the cultivar’s most recognizable signatures. Freshly opened flower can suggest grape candy, dark berries, tropical fruit, and creamy sweetness before the Green Lantern side begins to reveal itself. Earthy pine follows closely, bringing enough dry resin and forest character to keep the profile from becoming syrupy. Breaking the buds apart usually releases a sharper layer of fuel and Kush-like pungency.

Cookies describes its commercial Ridgeline Lantz as combining sweet purple candy and earthy pine, with a candy-Kush flavor and creamy finish. Laboratory testing of individual commercial batches also shows why the aroma can change noticeably between harvests. One Cookies sample was dominated by linalool, followed by limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and myrcene, demonstrating that the cultivar can express more floral and creamy chemistry than generalized terpene summaries suggest.

On the palate, fruit often arrives first. Grape and candy coat the tongue before pine, earthy resin, and gas become stronger through the exhale. A creamy backend softens the sharper Kush character and can leave behind a mixture of sweet fruit and fuel rather than one dominant aftertaste. This contrast is central to Lantz: it carries modern candy appeal without sacrificing the pungent, resinous qualities associated with Humboldt marijuana.
Growing Information

Lantz was originally developed in Southern Humboldt under Ridgeline Farms’ mixed-light and sun-grown cultivation system, making outdoor and greenhouse performance an important part of its history. The strain produces dense, rigid flowers with substantial trichome coverage and can develop dramatic purple pigmentation as maturity approaches. Strong floral density contributes to its visual appeal but also makes canopy airflow important during the final stages of bloom.

Preserved professional cultivation records generally place flowering around seven to eight weeks and describe yield as medium-high. Ridgeline Farms itself does not publish a standardized indoor flowering calendar or grams-per-square-meter number, so those figures should be regarded as cultivation benchmarks rather than universal breeder specifications. Environmental conditions, phenotype, vegetative time, root volume, and training strategy can significantly change final production.

Outdoors, the cultivar’s Humboldt background makes it well suited to mixed-light and full-sun production where warm days, cooler nights, and strong light intensity allow resin and coloration to develop fully. Harvest timing commonly falls during September into early October depending on planting date and local conditions. Dense cannabis flowers should be watched carefully when autumn humidity or rainfall increases, especially during the final weeks.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Lantz?

Lantz is Green Lantern × Ridgeline Runtz, bred by Ridgeline Farms in Southern Humboldt County. Jason Gellman and his father spent more than four years crossing, growing, and selecting plants before identifying the keeper phenotype that became the commercial cultivar.
Is Lantz indica or sativa?

Lantz is best described as a hybrid with an indica-leaning finish rather than a strain with a breeder-certified numerical ratio. Its early effects can feel uplifting, clear, and creative, while later stages become more physically relaxing and grounded.
How strong is Lantz weed?

Commercial flower commonly appears around 24–30% THC, although individual harvests may be lower or higher. Medical-market examples have been listed around 26–29% THC, while other retail flower has tested closer to the low 20s. The certificate of analysis for the actual batch is therefore the best potency guide.
What does Lantz strain taste like?

Expect purple candy, grape, sweet fruit, earthy pine, creamy Kush, and fuel. Ridgeline’s Green Lantern parent supplies much of the gas and pine character, while Ridgeline Runtz contributes fruit, sweetness, purple color, and resin.
Did Lantz win an Emerald Cup?

Yes. Lantz won first place in the Mixed Light Flower category at the 2023 Emerald Cup and also captured the Mixed Light Breeder’s Cup. Its parents were award winners as well: Green Lantern won licensed sungrown flower in 2018, and Ridgeline Runtz took first place in sungrown flower in 2019.
Final Thoughts on Lantz

Lantz is more than another Runtz-influenced cannabis hybrid. Its significance comes from the breeding history behind it. Ridgeline Farms combined two of its own Emerald Cup-winning cultivars, spent more than four years refining the cross, and eventually produced a plant that went on to win major awards of its own. Few modern marijuana strains can claim that kind of direct competition pedigree across both parents and offspring.

The finished flower justifies the attention. Purple candy and grape meet pine, creamy Kush, earth, and fuel; dense dark buds become coated in abundant resin; and the experience moves from cerebral euphoria toward comfortable full-body relaxation without immediately becoming overwhelming. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in contemporary Humboldt genetics, Lantz represents a particularly successful bridge between legacy gas, craft outdoor breeding, and the sweet purple flavor profiles that reshaped the modern weed market.
